Episode 123: Suddenly Like This? (4)
For a while, the two of them looked at each other in silence.
'Did Lata Proch have this side to him?'
The Phantom Brigade and its leader, Lata Proch.

In fact, Jin did not have a very good perception of them. When he was attacked by the assassins of the Phantom Brigade led by Fey, and when Lata later picked a fight with him, they both seemed foolish to Jin.
But who would have thought Lata had such insight? It was astonishing how well he saw through the situation and flow after the terrorist attack.
'No, no. No matter how I think about it, he didn't seem like such a smart person. Someone must have given Lata information or could be controlling him.'
Jin suppressed his admiration and shook his head inwardly.
He almost said, "Oh, is that so? I didn't expect such an excellent judgment," and let it pass too easily.
'Who could it be? Zipfel? Kinzelo? No, neither of those groups could have approached Lata. We were all tied down in Sword Emperor City.'
During the two weeks they stayed in Sword Emperor City, they naturally helped suppress the terror attacks and received intense investigations. Highran could not find any traces of Zipfel or Kinzelo.
'Zephyrin.'
Suddenly, the woman presumed to be a demon dragon came to his mind. Perhaps she was behind Lata.
Zephyrin's identity had not yet been fully revealed. Therefore, it would not be strange for her to be affiliated with either Zipfel or Kinzelo.
'But that would be too far-fetched. Even if Zephyrin had approached Lata with some purpose, it's impossible for Lata to act like this.'
The same was true for anyone other than Zephyrin.
It was hard to imagine that someone like the leader of the Phantom Brigade would give up his reputation to become someone's pawn.
If Jin were to refuse Lata right now and send him away, the weight of the name "Phantom Brigade Leader" would plummet into the abyss in an instant.

There were more than a few people who saw Jin and Lata in the reception room. Of course, it wouldn't be too difficult to silence them, but there would be no need to do so if they didn't form an alliance with Lata.
After a moment of contemplation, Jin concluded that Lata had come to him with his own free will and insight.
"Jin, what are you thinking so deeply about? Is there something strange about what I said?"
"No, it's not strange. It's just that you've read the situation so accurately that I can't help but wonder if it's really Lata who has gained all this insight."
"Hahaha!"
Lata burst into a hearty yet sharp laughter.

"Well, I can understand why you would think that from your perspective. My brother and I haven't shown ourselves in the best light so far. But Jin, I am also the leader of a group, a very well-respected leader at that."
Lata continued, looking at his index finger, which had been cut off but was now seamlessly reattached.
"Do you know why my 500 subordinates, who you admitted, followed me?"
It was an intriguing question. Five hundred was far too small a number to show off their power or to buy time in case of trouble in the Sword Garden.
Additionally, it was an ambiguous number compared to the scale of the Ghost Unit to consider that we brought this number with the intention of having us as subordinates.
"I don't know."
Slyly, Lata smiled.
"They were the 500 who never backed down even when dissuaded."
"What do you mean...?"
"When I said I would apologize to you by cutting off my index finger, they insisted on coming along, claiming they also had to offer their fingers to you."
This time, Jin's eyes couldn't help but widen.
Could it be true?
Lata had an expression in his eyes that left no room for doubt. Anyone who met Lata's gaze now would feel the pride he had.

"At first, many more subordinates said they would come with me. If I had brought all those guys, Runcandel would have thought we were here to wage war. Anyway, those who came along wouldn't back down, so I had no choice but to bring them."
"So if I ask them to, they will all cut off their index fingers?"
"That's right."
"That's a strange loyalty."
"It's hard to find anywhere else. They all made a fuss because they couldn't stand the thought of me being the only one to lose a finger. Now do you see how much of a respected leader I am?"
"Isn't there a way for everyone not to lose their fingers together?"
"Runcandel's 12th batch, if you allow it, it might be possible."
"What I mean is, wasn't there a way not to think of such a plan or practice it in the first place?"
"If a person commits a sin, shouldn't they pay the price? Especially if they want to get closer to the other party."
"A little while ago, you said that you were no different from a despicable and lowly beast, not a person."
"That's right. Is there a problem with that?"
Jin shook his head with a mix of indescribable feelings.
And for a moment, he recalled the faces of Lata's subordinates who were taken away by Murakan.
They all had expressionless faces. Maybe they would lose a part of their body that had been attached to them for a lifetime, just like their lord.
'Lata Proch was not an ordinary person.'
If everything he said so far was true, Lata was a person who fit the role of a great leader.
No matter how outstanding Lata's martial arts skills were, there was a reason he had completely taken control of the Ghost Unit at such a young age.
"I have one question, Sir Lata."
"What is it?"
"Why did you act so third-rate at the Geomhwangseong banquet?"
To Jin, Lata Proch today and that day were completely different people.
"Although I am a competent and excellent leader in most situations, there are times when my imperfect personality is revealed. For example, when my only blood relative is taken hostage."
"Your sibling is being treated well enough that there would be no problem even if the strictest prisoner of war regulations were applied."
"Well, I appreciate it, but it's not a big issue as long as my strong sibling is alive and receiving enough treatment. And also... it can happen when I lose a subordinate who is most precious to me."
Fey recalled the day he was attacked.
'Was it Grimol?'
The most overwhelming, or perhaps the only person among the Ghost Unit assassins who had given him trouble. He had wielded a sword far superior to Fey's.
"I let him go without pain. The final stroke of the sword that Grimol, the assassin, showed me seemed like something brilliant to me too. He tried to save Fey Proch until the end."

"...I've always been curious about how my friend's end would be, but it seems he had an honorable death for a mercenary. Though we spent a long time together, Grimol was more of a knight than an assassin."
Lata, with his eyes gently closed, appeared to be commemorating Grimol for a moment.

"Looking back, I paid a hefty price for underestimating you then. I should not have taken the request in the first place, and if I had, I should have formed a team with the best assassins, including myself. So this time, I'm trying to make the best choice without making any mistakes. Please help me."
There was a sincere feeling in his calm tone.
Of course, the sincere feeling he now had didn't mean he could pick up the careless remarks he made recently.
However, Jin knew well that everyone could make mistakes.
"Sir Lata Proch."
"Go ahead."
"If you really want to form an alliance with me, show me your trust. Mere verbal repentance and meaningless bloodshed by cutting off fingers won't allow us to be on the same boat."
Lata finally smiled as if he had thrown off his oppressive clothes.
"What do you want? What would you like me to show you?"
"Initially, the Ghost Unit and I met as targets to be eliminated and as assassins."
At that, Lata's pupils narrowed.
"If this bad relationship is to change into a connection, shouldn't the necks of those who ordered me killed be presented before me?"
Assassinate the Runcandel elders.
Of course, it was one of the worst requests that an assassin group could receive.
"It would have been better if you had taken their necks and brought them to me before I said anything. I know why Sir Lata didn't do that."
As if being pricked, Lata flinched and gave an awkward smile.
"It must be because you didn't want to take a risk. If you brought the elders' heads and I didn't accept the alliance, it would mean you have no way out."
"...Once again, I realize that you are extraordinary."

"Also, even if I were to welcome you with open arms after you brought the heads of those old men, you might have doubted whether the 12th Generation could protect the Ghost Unit from Runcandel's retaliation."
Squeaking, Jin stood up from his chair. He then slowly moved behind Lata, who couldn't stand up and remained seated.
A few seconds later, Jin's hand gently touched Lata's shoulder, feeling as cold and endless as a reaper's scythe.
"Take a risk, Lata Proch, if you truly trust me, if you are sure that I will be Runcandel's loser."
With an icy cold voice, chills ran down his spine.
"I'll give you a week."
Jin spoke as he removed his hand from Lata's shoulder.

"Within that time, bring me the heads of those who wanted me dead. Don't even think about taking it lightly, I'm telling you to commit to the task. I will take responsibility for the aftermath. Do you understand?"
Lata nodded heavily.
'12th Generation, this is an unexpected development...'
Of course, Lata sincerely believed that Jin would eventually become the head of Runcandel.
However, he didn't think Jin held significant power within Runcandel at the moment. Therefore, the plan was to join hands first and then gradually help Jin expand his influence.
But now, a situation had been formed where he had to become an enemy of the 'current Runcandel' within a week.
'Even though I planned to side with the 12th Generation, this leaves no way out.'
Show your trust.
As Lata mulled over Jin's words in his head, Jin spoke again.
"If the deadline passes and the heads are not delivered, I will assume that Sir Lata has joined hands with another force instead of me. That means we become enemies again."
"That won't happen..."
"Please, make a wise choice."
